stories.title: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo spreads to an eighth province
stories.summary: Two Ebola cases were recorded in North Ubangi, a Congolese province bordering the Central African Republic, making it the eighth province affected, according to Reuters citing two health officials. The outbreak has caused more than 9,000 cases and 4,441 deaths, per figures released Wednesday. It is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no vaccine or treatment, and the WHO expects a first vaccine clinical trial in the DRC by the end of October. Kenya announced its second case on Wednesday, and Congolese authorities had not yet announced the new province.

stories.title: Houthi militias strike presidential palace in Aden, Yemen
stories.summary: Houthi militias struck the presidential palace in Aden, the seat of Yemen's Saudi-backed government, and five people died, including two of the prime minister's bodyguards. Yemeni officials said the prime minister was unharmed. The attack follows recent Houthi strikes on Saudi oil infrastructure and nearly two dozen attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which Saudi officials say killed 17 people and injured more than 300.

stories.title: Pentagon reportedly to delay report on Iranian school strike; Hormuz ship attacks continue
stories.summary: Bloomberg reported that top Pentagon officials intend to withhold an internal report on the bombing of a school in southern Iran until after the U.S. midterm elections at the earliest. The strike killed at least 156 people: 120 children, 26 teachers and the remainder parents. Separately, another oil tanker was struck near the Strait of Hormuz, and maritime officials counted 12 vessels attacked in and around the strait from October 5 to 11, the highest pace since the U.S. began its naval blockade of Iranian ports.

stories.title: Dow edges higher as tech sell-off lingers after hot inflation data
stories.summary: On October 15 the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 52,177.69, up 556.21 points (1.08%), while the S&P 500 rose 0.33% to 7,744.06 and the Nasdaq gained 0.08% to 26,713.02. Wednesday's hotter-than-expected Consumer Price Index had revived fears of Federal Reserve rate hikes and hit AI and semiconductor stocks. Treasury yields fell in the afternoon, with the 10-year yield dropping about 10.5 basis points to 5.085%. Gains came from consumer, healthcare and financial stocks while tech lagged.

stories.title: Human brain still processes language under general anesthesia, Nature study finds
stories.summary: Baylor College of Medicine researchers led by Dr. Sameer Sheth used Neuropixels probes to record hundreds of individual hippocampal neurons in epilepsy surgery patients under general anesthesia, in a study published in Nature. Neurons responded differently to unexpected tones and improved at distinguishing them over the experiment, suggesting plasticity. Neural activity also carried information distinguishing nouns, verbs and adjectives and could be used to predict upcoming words. The study used one type of anesthesia and only the hippocampus, so it is unclear whether similar processing occurs during sleep or coma.

stories.title: Arctic sea ice reaches 10th-lowest minimum on record; winter peak ties record low
stories.summary: NASA and the National Snow and Ice Data Center report that Arctic sea ice reached its 2026 minimum on September 12 at about 4.6 million square kilometers, tying 2008, 2010 and 2025 for the 10th-lowest in the satellite record. The March 2026 maximum tied March 2025 for the lowest winter peak on record. September extent has been relatively stable over the past decade, with increased cloud cover cited as one factor, but multiyear ice has declined and thinner first-year ice is more vulnerable to melting. Scientists project the Arctic could be essentially ice-free in summer at least once before the middle of the century.
